units.translation: otherwise, if not, or because if it were not so: in such places it can also be translated as 'for'. But it is often used with a following interrogative τίς [who?]: on which see Thes. vol. 3 p. 1454.
i.e. as soon as.
although in such places 'after' is also suitable.
Thus it is commonly read from the apograph instead of ἐπιγένοιτ' [might come upon], which is in M. Aeschylus had written the neuter, about which see under προκλύω.
As soon as the gods began their wrath
as quickly as possible
For when you came to the Molossian plains
And when he became sound of mind
When you came down to the city
And when I arose
And when the light of the sun had set
When indeed the white-horsed day had covered all the earth
And when the army had ceased from its many cries to the gods
And when another remedy for the bitter storm—the seer cried out
And when he entered the yoke-strap of necessity
When often in his father's halls with well-spread tables he sang
And when the bright light of the sun rose
When I first saw the city of Ilium
And when I remembered the relentless toils
And when wretched Orestes had reached the height of many woes
This is the tenth year since Priam's great adversary
And time—when he had passed his prime
A torch of equal age, when coming from his mother he cried out
No indeed, since the fortunes of my brother Atlas also wear me down
Let me be sick with this sickness, since it is best
Since he is eager, it is necessary to speak
Since you are eager, I will not oppose
Since the god strongly urges the matter, let it go with a fair wind
And he was a god-counselled man, since he well commanded the army
Since I have come from below, persuaded by your laments—speak
Since old fear of your mind stands in the way, speak
But since hearing beforehand would be a release, let it be welcomed
He is deemed just, since the child pursues a winged bird
And since I have been brought to this point of listening to you, I will go to the halls of the house
And I am such a one, since I am at a loss
Since you think to do and say these things, you will soon know
Act, fatten yourself, defiling justice, since it is possible
Since you are present as escorts of this supplication to me, become also of these things—I bring in addition
counsellors about
Since lifting him up greatly, double and triple—willingly he will repay
Sleep with him in death, since you love this man
And they were born for the sake of evils, since they inhabit evil darkness
And since you know, learn also to be careless
Let us begin the dance, since it has been decided to display a hateful muse
And since this matter has fallen upon us here, I will establish the ordinance for all time
Since a young man rides me down, an old woman, I wait to be a hearer of this judgment
Since the vote of the Argives is complete, children, take courage
It seems I will drag you, tearing you by the hair, since you do not hear sharply
It is necessary to pray to the Argives, since they are saviours not in doubt
And you will have no stone to pick from the ground, since every place is soft
Since a god—perhaps he would come with a more favourable wind
